ideas.title: Lockstep Canals
ideas.cad_prompt:
REQUIREMENT: The canal board, the loading sill, and all 40 stones (36 lock-stones plus 4 font-stones) must be produced as 42 separate, freely liftable, physically unconnected components. No stone is fused to the board, to the loading sill, or to any other stone. In the exported model each stone sits inside its well or slot with a continuous surrounding air gap of at least 1mm on every side and is not merged, welded, or boolean-unioned with the socket it occupies.

COMPONENT 1 - Canal board. Quantity 1. A single rigid slab measuring 366 x 366 x 15mm overall (footprint including four projecting edge spurs). The top face is milled with a 6x6 grid of 36 square wells, each well 42 x 42mm in plan and 4mm deep, arranged on a 44mm center-to-center pitch, centered on the board. One additional square well, identical in size (42 x 42 x 4mm deep), projects outward from the midpoint of each of the board's four outer edges (4 spur wells total, one per edge). One open-topped rectangular draw bin is recessed into one corner of the board: interior cavity 170 x 90mm in plan x 36mm deep, solid walls and floor, top fully open with no lid, cover, or bridging material spanning the opening, reachable by a hand entering straight down from directly above with nothing overhanging the opening. The board is otherwise a single continuous solid body; the wells and the bin are subtractive cavities cut into it, not separate parts.

COMPONENT 2 - Lock-stones. Quantity 36 loose, individually printed flat square tiles, each 40 x 40 x 8mm. Each stone belongs to one of 4 shape families defined by which of its 4 edges carry a carved trench running from that edge to a shared center hub: Straight family (2 opposite edges grooved, 2 plain edges), Corner family (2 adjacent edges grooved, 2 plain edges), Tee family (3 edges grooved, 1 plain edge), Cross family (all 4 edges grooved, 0 plain edges). Each of the 4 shape families exists in 3 level variants distinguished by tally-notch count: level 1, level 2, level 3. Each shape-and-level combination has exactly 3 identical copies (4 shapes x 3 levels x 3 copies = 36 stones total). On every stone, each grooved edge is cut with a straight trench 5mm wide x 3mm deep with a rounded concave floor, running from that edge inward to a single shared center hub where all of that stone's trenches meet; plain edges carry no trench and are flat. Along the rim of every grooved edge, cut a row of triangular tally notches: the number of notches on every grooved edge of a given stone equals that stone's level (1, 2, or 3); each notch is 2mm wide x 1.5mm deep, and notches are spaced 3mm apart center-to-center along the edge. Every outer edge of every lock-stone (all 4 edges, grooved or plain) carries a 2mm x 45-degree chamfer running the full edge length. Each lock-stone sits loose and unattached inside one 42 x 42 x 4mm board well or one 44 x 44 x 3mm loading-sill slot, with 1mm of plan clearance on each side, and stands proud of the surrounding surface by the difference between the 8mm stone height and the socket depth, free to be lifted straight up by hand.

COMPONENT 3 - Font-stones. Quantity 4, each 40 x 40 x 8mm, same outer envelope and edge chamfer as lock-stones. Each font-stone has exactly one grooved edge, cut with the same 5mm wide x 3mm deep rounded trench as a lock-stone but at level 0: zero tally notches along that edge's rim. That single trench leads from the edge inward to a round scooped reservoir at the tile's center: 8mm diameter x 3mm deep, concave floor. The other 3 edges of every font-stone are plain, with no trench and no notches. Near the corner diagonally opposite the grooved edge, each font-stone carries a row of pierced through-holes, each 3mm diameter, spaced 6mm apart center-to-center: one font-stone has 1 hole, one has 2 holes, one has 3 holes, one has 4 holes, so that all four owner-hole counts (1, 2, 3, 4) are each represented on exactly one font-stone. Font-stones seat loosely in the board's spur wells with the same 1mm-per-side clearance and proud-standing behavior described for lock-stones.

COMPONENT 4 - Loading sill. Quantity 1, a plank 240 x 60 x 12mm. Cut into its top face are 5 square cupped slots arranged in a single row, each 44 x 44mm in plan x 3mm deep, spaced 46mm apart center-to-center. Each of the 5 slots is a distinct depression with its own surrounding lip; the slots do not merge into one continuous trough. Each slot loosely seats one lock-stone or font-stone with the clearances described above.

unstated_in_spec: Which of the board's four corners hosts the draw bin is not specified in the spec; the prompt leaves this as a single unspecified corner rather than assigning one.
Font-stone owner-hole spacing (center-to-center distance between the 1-4 pierced holes) is not given in the spec; 6mm spacing was assigned and should be treated as a placeholder value.

ideas.title: Sluice Row
ideas.cad_prompt:
REQUIREMENT: The trough board and all 48 seed-weights must exist as 49 discrete, freely liftable, physically separate components. No seed-weight is fused to the board or to any other seed-weight; each sits loose inside a well with a continuous air gap around its full circumference, free to be lifted or poured out by hand.

COMPONENT 1 - Trough board. Quantity 1, a single rigid slab 380 x 170 x 24mm overall, with a rolled bullnose edge (rounded profile, 4mm radius) running the full perimeter of the top edge. Twelve small circular wells are recessed into the top face in two parallel rows of 6, each well 26mm diameter x 16mm deep, with a 2mm rounded fillet at the rim. On the interior wall of every one of the 12 small wells, engrave a single continuous capacity ring: 1mm wide x 0.5mm deep, running horizontally around the full interior circumference of the well at a height 9mm up from the well floor; this ring is a distinct engraved groove line, separate and visually distinguishable from the well's rounded rim fillet at the top opening. Two additional circular store wells are recessed one into each short end of the board: 55mm diameter x 20mm deep each, visibly larger in both diameter and depth than the 12 small wells, with the same 2mm rim fillet but no capacity ring engraved on their interior walls. The board is otherwise a single continuous solid; the 14 wells are subtractive cavities cut into it, not separate parts.

COMPONENT 2 - Seed-weights. Quantity 48 loose cylinders total, all 7mm tall, in 3 diameter groups distinguished only by diameter: 16 small cylinders at 10mm diameter, 16 medium cylinders at 14mm diameter, 16 large cylinders at 18mm diameter. All three groups share the identical 7mm height so that pile height inside a well is a reliable visual gauge against the well's capacity ring regardless of which diameters are mixed in a pile. Each seed-weight is a plain right circular cylinder with a 1mm edge chamfer on both the top and bottom rim. Each seed-weight sits loose inside a well: an 18mm-diameter large seed-weight resting inside a 26mm-diameter small well has a minimum 3mm radial gap between its edge and the well wall on every side (13mm well radius minus 9mm seed radius = 4mm radial clearance), sufficient for two-finger pinch removal; the smaller diameter groups have proportionally greater clearance in the same well.

unstated_in_spec: Exact chamfer size on the seed-weight top/bottom rim edges is not given in the spec; 1mm was assigned as a placeholder to avoid a sharp-edge default.

ideas.title: Tidepool Stones
ideas.cad_prompt:
REQUIREMENT: The tide basin board and all 64 shell-lens discs must exist as 65 discrete, freely liftable, physically separate components. No disc is fused to the board or to any other disc; each disc sits loose in its hollow with a continuous air gap around its full circumference, free to be lifted and flipped by hand.

COMPONENT 1 - Tide basin board. Quantity 1, a single rigid slab 260 x 260 x 18mm overall. The top face carries an 8x8 grid of 64 shallow circular hollows, each 30mm diameter x 3mm deep, arranged on a 32mm center-to-center pitch. Every pair of orthogonally adjacent hollows is separated by a continuous raised dividing ridge standing 2mm proud of the hollow floor, with a 1mm fillet along the ridge's top edge; the ridge network forms a continuous grid spanning the full board so all 64 hollows read as individually bounded depressions rather than a single flat plate. The board is otherwise a single continuous solid; the hollows are subtractive cavities and the ridges are the raised material remaining between them, not separate parts.

COMPONENT 2 - Shell-lens discs. Quantity 64, all identical, each a biconvex-profile puck 28mm diameter x 7mm tall (the edge profile curves outward from a thin rim toward a thicker center on both faces). One face of every disc, the Ridge face, is engraved with exactly 4 concentric rings: each ring 1mm wide x 0.8mm deep, spaced 2mm apart, centered on the disc. The opposite face of the same disc, the Fan face, is engraved with exactly 8 straight radial grooves: each groove 1mm wide x 0.8mm deep, running from the disc's center to its rim, spaced evenly at 45-degree intervals around the disc. Every one of the 64 discs carries both engraved faces on the same physical disc, one motif per side; there is no separate part per face. Each disc seats loose in one 30mm-diameter x 3mm-deep hollow, giving a minimum 1mm radial clearance on every side (15mm hollow radius minus 14mm disc radius = 1mm gap, exceeding the 0.8mm minimum), and stands 4mm proud of the surrounding ridge (7mm disc height minus 3mm hollow depth), enough for a two-finger pinch-and-flip.

unstated_in_spec: The exact curvature radius of the disc's biconvex edge profile is not given in the spec; the prompt describes the profile qualitatively (thin rim to thicker center) without assigning a numeric radius.
